Commentary.Commentary: So that is it from the final game of the series. Morgan and his teammates now lift the cup, spilling champagne everywhere. Happy moments for the home side. Australia on the other hand, have a lot to improve. Cricketing action though does not end here as you can catch all the action from the second day of the third Test between Windies and Sri Lanka starting in a short while. Till then, take care and goodbye.

English skipper, Eoin Morgan says there are massive positives to take from today. Mentions the lower order stood up when the top order failed. Applauds the way Buttler played. Further adds he has forced his way back into the Test team and is an important member of the ODI team. Admits it is the first time they failed in this series with the bat as a group and he would not want to repeat that. States that this was a tremendous fightback.

Australian skipper, Tim Paine says they have been taught a lesson from a world-class outfit. Credits the way Jos Buttler played after they had them under pressure. He feels they bowled a touch wide to Rashid and Buttler. At the halfway mark he thought the total was not enough but their bowlers came out and did their job really well. Acknowledges the way Short and Carey played. He reckons Stanlake is a very talented bowler. Ends by thanking the crowd for the support they have shown.

Man of the Match and Series, Jos Buttler feels great about his performance today. Further adds they bowled really well but did not quite match it up with the bat. Says they just needed a partnership and Adil Rashid hung in well with him. Ends by saying he was ready to run the twos but not the ones when Jake Ball came out to bat.

England will be over the moon with this series win. They have got a clean sweep over the World Champions and that will bolster them as a unit. It was a gallant performance by their batsmen throughout (barring today) where they completely outclassed the Kangaroos. On the bowling front, there is still scope for improvement though as they can become even more clinical. Their next assignment is against India and that will truly judge their form, ability and quality.

Earlier in the day, a solid opening partnership between Aaron Finch and Travis Head was followed by a complete disintegration of the Aussie batting line-up. One by one the batsmen were sent to the pavilion and the collapse meant that the visitors ended with only 205 on the board. The Aussie bowlers probably bowled their best in this series today but the victory just wasn't meant to be. Jos Buttler stood like a rock in front of them and the 9th wicket partnership killed most of their hopes. Still, a word of praise for Billy Stanlake, he bowled his heart out and looked menacing.

For the visitors, it was a case of so near and yet so far. Defending a paltry total, Billy Stanlake came out all guns blazing and England were soon reduced to 5 for 50. With their backs to the wall and defeat looming large, Jos Buttler took the charge and decided to play as per the situation where he had to curb his natural game. He kept on losing partners at the other end but that didn't deter him a single bit. With the home side tottering on 114/8, Buttler finally found an able ally in Adil Rashid. Together the pair stitched in an 81-run stand to put England in a winning position out of nowhere. It did get close towards the end but Jos kept his cool to first score his century and then steer his team over the line where a sweet whitewash moment was waiting for them.

England have done it. They have registered their first whitewash over Australia in a 5-match bilateral series. The English players are delighted. Jos Buttler cannot hide his smile. Eoin Morgan is on the ground shaking hands with the Australian players. This series has been played in good spirits. Another defeat for Australia, however, they managed to push England this time around.

FOUR! ENGLAND WIN BY 1 WICKET! A length ball in the zone outside off, Jos crunches it through covers for a boundary. Buttler leaps in joy and the crowd has gone bonkers. What a win! What a terrific win! Jos Buttler, take a bow. Smiles all around in the English camp. Mission 5-0 accomplished.
In line of the stumps, Buttler shows his back leg first to put off the bowler but then stays back and defends it down.
A length ball on middle, Buttler helps it through mid-wicket but denies the single. Taking no chance now.
The field is up now.
Looks for the yorker but fails to execute it properly. A full toss on off, Buttler pushes it firmly down to long off for a single. 2 needed more. England's game to lose.
Wrong line, it's full and on middle and leg, Ball flicks it behind square leg and they cross for a run. Buttler is back on strike, England 3 away, can he hit a boundary?
A length ball on off, Ball stays back and pushes it to covers.
This is pressure and Ball is dealing with it quite well. Gets a fullish ball on off, once again moving in and he drives it to covers.
Very full and swinging back into the batsman, Ball does well to keep it out towards covers.

What? Just a single. Has Buttler misjudged this? A full ball around off, it's been driven down to long off and he crosses for a run. It stays that way as the fielder is quite active in returning the ball back.
Kane Richardson to bowl the 48th over...
Gets behind the line of the delivery and defends. HUGE CHEER from the English crowd. Well done, Jake Ball. He has survived. Over to Buttler now.
Full and on middle, flicked away but straight to short fine leg.
Agar delivers it around off, Ball brings his bat down in time to keep it out safely.
Very full and on off, Ball drives it through the line and it goes on one bounce to the cover fielder.
Quicker and on the pads, kept out safely.
Ooohhh...misses the outside edge by a whisker. A flatter and shorter ball just outside off, Ball stays back to punch it through but misses.
Ball on strike... 5 runs needed... a six anyone?

SIX! Boom! Great way to reach his 6th ODI hundred, 2nd against Australia! Stoinis serves a shortish length ball outside off, Jos stays inside the crease and launches it over the long on fence for a biggie. He reaches his milestone but that will mean Ball will be on strike for the next over. What will happen?
Jake Ball is the next man in. 11 more needed. He is off strike for now as the batsmen crossed.

OUT! Rashid loses his cool eventually and holes out! Stoinis bowls a cross-seam delivery, angling down the leg side, Rashid tries to flick it on the leg side but it takes the top edge balloons in the air towards fine leg. Billy Stanlake comes running in and grabs the catch by diving forward. This game takes another turn.
Action replay of the previous delivery. Rashid holding his head under pressure. Nothing fancy from him.
Bowls it in the line of the stumps, Rashid brings his bat and pad together in defense.
A length ball again, around off, Buttler opens the face of the bat and pushes it through covers for a single.
Angles in a length ball on middle, Buttler plays it down from the crease towards mid on. Stays on 97!
Fullish and on middle, eased down to mid on to end the over. Well batted, Adil. A maiden won't hurt England.
Flighted full ball on off, defended again by Rashid.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

Almost trapped him in front! An arm ball landing on a fuller length around middle, Rashid brings his bat down in time to keep it out off the inside half of the bat. Had he missed, he was a plumb lbw candidate.
Quicker and flatter outside off, Rashid plays it down with an angled bat to short third man.
Fuller and around leg, played off the pads to short mid-wicket.
Slower delivery, a bit short around off, Rashid goes on his toes and turns it in the gap behind square leg for a run. 12 more needed.
Good length ball landing around off, shaping back in a bit, Rashid remains on the back foot and defends it down.
Too full and on off, driven straight towards covers who misfielded and allowed a run.
Tim Paine comes up to the stumps.
FOUR! Timing and placement. Buttler moves on to 96! It's full and sliding down the leg side, Jos closes the face of the bat at the right time and flicks it beautifully through mid-wicket.
Angles in a fuller length ball on off, Buttler drives it down the ground but straight to the mid off fielder.
Bowls it full and outside off, Rashid has his front foot right in line of the delivery as he drives it square of the wicket on the off side. A delightful single.
Another run towards sweeper cover and now the equation is 19 off 42 balls.
Arm ball on off, staying a bit low, Buttler moves back and forces it to sweeper cover for a run.
A low full toss this time, on off, Jos drives but finds the extra cover fielder.
Agar is once again on the shorter side and Buttler smacks it through covers. Carey in the deep makes a fine diving stop, thereby saving a couple for his team.
Flatter and shorter on off, a gentle punch off the back foot by Rashid and it goes to deep cover for a run.
Every run is cheered now. A full ball on middle, Jos has worked it down to long on for a run.
On a length around off, Adil covers the line and blocks it to end the over. The crowd has found its voice and is now singing on top of its tonsils. England 25 away from 5-0!
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman. They pick up a single.

FOUR! This is in the slot for Buttler and he has driven it with great timing through covers. The sweeper in the deep moves across to his left to stop the ball but fails in his attempt. England continue to cruise under this partnership.
What a shot! Nice way to bring up the highest 9th wicket partnership for England in ODIs against Australia. A pitched up delivery outside off has been driven smartly through point for three runs.
Shortish and outside off, Rashid goes back and defends it down.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Takes a positive stride forward to a full ball and strokes it towards wide long off for a single.
Quicker and flatter on middle, Rashid gets back and defends it down safely.
Mid on comes up.
Tossed up ball on middle and leg, Buttler gives it the full face of his bat and forces it down past the bowler for a single at long on.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Stays back inside the crease and punches it towards the fielder on the leg side.

EDGY FOUR! Ashton Agar can do nothing and just smiles. An arm ball by him, a bit short around off and it skids in after landing. Buttler hangs on the back foot as he tries to punch it through covers. But it catches the outside edge and runs past the keeper to the third man fence.
Powerplay 3 signalled. Now 5 fielders can be placed outside the circle. Also, Ashton Agar comes back into the attack.
Taps a length ball down to point and takes a run. Once again Jos keeps strike with himself on the final ball.
Tries to drive it through covers but it takes the inner half of the bat and rolls to mid on.

FOUR! Cracking shot! Buttler is doing it for England. Gets a fuller length delivery in his half and he has drilled it through the line. It races away to the fence after beating the dive by Agar from mid off. The 50-run stand comes up, potentially a match-winning one for the home team.
Gets behind the line of the delivery and blocks it on the leg side, straight towards short mid-wicket.
Wide! Slips a full ball down the leg side, Buttler tries his best to get some bat behind it but misses. Good diving take by Paine to his left.
Good length ball on off, defended off the back foot.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Quicker one on off, Adil brings his bat down in time to keep it out. No wickets for Lyon but he threatened to pick a few. Ends with 10-0-32-0!
Gets well forward to a full ball in defense but it takes spin and goes off the inside edge to backward square leg.
Loopy and full on off, Adil is on the front foot in defense.
Short and outside off, Buttler rocks back and slaps it square of the wicket on the off side. It's uppish but there is no fielder in that region inside the ring. An easy single.
Strides forward to a full ball and knocks it down to long on for one.
Tossed up ball on middle, Jos goes on the back foot and works it through mid-wicket for a run.
This time finds the gap through covers and retains strike with a single. Huge cheer from the crowd.
Plays a good looking drive to a full ball but finds the cover fielder.

Run out appeal against Jos Buttler has been taken upstairs... NOT OUT! The full length dive has saved him. A rising delivery around off, Jos goes on his toes and helps it through square leg. Wants the second run but loses his footing a bit while turning. Still goes on with it and then dives to get inside the crease as the throw comes to the keeper who takes the bails off. It's referred upstairs but much to the delight of the English fans, Jos is safe.

Four leg byes! Stanlake spears a full ball in line of the stumps, angling down though after landing around middle, Buttler tries to flick but misses and it brushes his pads before screaming away to the fine leg fence.
A speedy delivery again, on the shorter side outside off, Rashid extends his arms and guides it down to third man for a run.
Back of a length delivery on off, Rashid jumps on his back foot and defends it down safely.
Floated and on off, Jos defends it off his front foot. 5 from the over, no such pressure on England in terms of the asking run rate.
Flighted delivery, again too straight by Lyon and Rashid clips it behind square leg for a single. 150 comes up for England, needing another 56 for a win.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. One run added to the total.
Turns it off his pads in front of square leg and crosses.

Skidding away from the batsman from around off, Rashid takes a big stride forward and then opens the face of the bat to guide it past short third man. Stanlake gives it the chase, runs with the ball, tries racing with it and then decides to pick it up to kill the chase. A couple taken.
Strides forward to a full ball and pushes it towards mid-wicket.
Goes on the back foot to a good length ball and defends to end the over.
On a length around off, defended off the back foot.
FOUR! Boom! Stanlake bangs in a 90 mph short delivery on middle, Buttler decides to fight fire with fire as he goes deep inside the crease and pulls it thunderously to the deep mid-wicket fence.
Stanlake digs in a short ball on off, Rashid is early into his pull shot and it goes off his right forearm to covers. They steal a leg bye.
Width on offer outside off, it's run down to third man where Stoinis makes a stop with a tumble. A couple taken.
Back of a length delivery on off, Buttler punches it off his back foot to sweeper cover for one. This is now the highest score by a number 6 batsman in ODIs at Old Trafford.
Good try by the bowler! Goes for the toe-crusher but ends up bowling a low full toss. Rashid jams it out to mid-wicket.
Eases this full ball down to long on and takes a run. Runs required is below 70 now.
Good line and length to end the over. On off, Buttler gives it respect as he defends it to covers.
Good length outside off, Rashid guides it down to third man and takes a run.
Down the leg side, Stoinis bowls the second wide of the over.
Back of a length on middle, Rashid with a straight bat defends it.
Back of a length on off, Jos drops it towards covers and takes a single.
A bumper wide outside off, Buttler lets it be and the umpire signals a wide.
A single to end the over! 9 from it and more importantly for England, Buttler retains strike. He jams this yorker out to the off side and takes a run. 74 more needed.
Another couple! This is turning out to be a good over for England! Buttler times this through covers and bags a brace.
The batsman dances down the track and does well to block the ball.

FOUR! Well bowled, well played but perhaps Stanlake could have put in a better effort. Buttler shuffles across the stumps, like he has been doing in this innings. Richardson spears it full and on middle. Buttler gets bat to it in time. Deflects it fine down the leg side. Billy runs to his right, dives but can't stop it. A boundary results.
Lovely use of the wrists! On middle, Rashid flicks it over square leg for a run.
A single by Buttler on the first ball. Something the Aussies won't mind. On a length around off, Buttler taps it towards covers for a run.
Hits the length again on off, Rashid goes back and defends it. Just 2 from the over.
Wide outside off, Rashid mistimes it to covers.
Length again outside off, Rashid guides it towards point.
Back of a length on off, kept out.
Back of a length on off, Rashid opens the face of the bat and guides it through point. Carey does well to run to his left and save two runs for his side.
Stoinis who is back into the attack lands it on a length around off, Rashid covers the line of the delivery and defends it onto the ground.
Drops it on a length around off, Buttler gets across the stumps and defends it down.

FOUR! A well-constructed fifty by Buttler. Richardson bowls it on a good length outside off, Buttler stays back and eases it down to third man for a boundary, first for him since the Lunch break. He has been very sensible with his approach in the run chase, curbing his natural way of batting. This is also his slowest half century in ODIs, beating the previous one against India which came off 59 balls. Can he drag England to victory?
Chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Pitches it full and around off, Buttler drives it off his front foot towards mid off.
In the channel outside off, Jos lets it be.
A length ball angling down the leg side, Buttler gets across to work it away on the leg side but misses. It deflects off his pads to fine leg for a couple of leg byes.
Shorter in length on off, Rashid stands tall and defends it onto the ground.
Wide outside off, Rashid does not play at it.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Short on middle, Buttler rides on top of the bounce and pulls it all along the ground through square leg for a run.
Lovely stuff! Full, just outside the eye line of the batsman. Buttler is drawn into the cover-drive with not a lot of foot movement. He gets beaten.
Back of a length on off, Buttler stands tall and defends it to point.
Billy Stanlake is back on. Paine is going for the kill here. Probably the ideal move at the moment.
A dot to end a very successful over! A run and two wickets from it. It is bowled outside off, Rashid does what the batsmen who got out should have. Left it.
No hat-trick but a very good delivery! Better than the ones he took the wickets with. On a length outside off, tails back in a touch. Rashid lunges forward and keeps it out.
Adil Rashid walks out to the middle. He will be facing the hat-trick ball.
Drinks!

OUT! Two-in-two for Richardson. Plunkett comes and Plunkett goes. Another ball which is full and wide outside off. A ball which you can shoulder your arms to. But Liam slashes at it, not a shot you want to play on your first ball. The ball takes the outside edge and goes low towards the right of Paine who dives and takes it. The players appeal and this time the umpire does hear it as he raises his finger. Richardson is now on a hat-trick and the Australians are all pumped up at the moment.
Liam Plunkett walks out to the middle.

OUT! There is a spike on Snicko and Curran has been given his marching orders. The bowling change does the trick for Australia. Richardson bowls a sucker ball outside off, Curran cannot resist and he goes after it. There seems to be a sound as the ball passes the bat. The players make a huge appeal but the umpire shakes his head. Paine signals for the 'T'. They go upstairs and Snicko shows a spike. The on-field call has to be overturned and Australia can sniff it now.

Another review! This time it is for a caught behind. The umpire does not think there is an edge but Paine is very confident. There was also a noise as the ball passed the bat. Curran is the man in question.
Slaps this through covers for a run.
OOOO! Bowls a similar delivery to which he got a wicket with. Outside off, Buttler goes after it but misses.
Kane Richardson is back on.

FOUR! A half-tracker to start the over and a one to end it. It was on middle, once again Curran has all the time to go back and pick his spot. Goes over mid-wicket and gets a boundary. An expensive first over by Short. The question here is, was there a need to bowl him?
Stoppage in play! Well, there is a big balloon on the field. Stoinis picks it up and tries to throw it in the stand. He fails to do so. The guard then does what Marcus could not.
Gives it air and bowls it on off, Curran drives it to covers.
Floats it up on middle, Buttler goes back and tucks it around the corner for a run.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat. The batsmen have run through for a single.
This is bowled outside off, the batsman does not fiddle with it.
SIX! A long hop to start with. Curran has all the the time in the world to rock back, pick his spot and deposit it over the long on fence for a biggie.
D'Arcy Short is into the attack.
Length again on off, slightest of width on offer. Buttler opens the face of the bat and guides it through point for a brace. 100 up for England. They need another 105 runs.
Persists with the line outside off, Buttler camps back and defends it onto the ground.
Hits the length on off, Buttler pushes it to mid off.
Back of a length outside off, Curran guides it towards point for a run. England are now one short of 100.
Worked through mid-wicket for a single.
Steps down the wicket and gets a length ball on off. Buttler defends it out.
Floats it up on off, kept out.
Flatter outside off, the batsman lets it be.

Howzat? The answer to that question is not out. Lyon fires this one on the middle pole. It goes on with the arm as Curran tries to flick. He misses to get hit on the front pad. The players appeal but the umpire shakes his head. Tim Paine walks up to his bowler and the two have a chat. In the end, they decide to take it upstairs. Time for the replays. They show that there is no inside edge and Hawk Eye shows it to be clipping the leg pole. Umpire's call stays but the good thing for Australia is they do not lose a review. England will breathe a sigh of relief as they cannot lose a wicket at this time.
Guides it towards point and runs to the other end.
Slower through the air on middle, Buttler flicks it to mid-wicket.
Floats it up on off, Buttler lunges and keeps it out.
A bumper to end the over, Curran does the right thing by evading it.
Shorter in length on off, Curran stands tall and pushes it to mid off. He just has to survive out there with Buttler.
Hits the length on off, Curran off the middle, pushes it to mid off.
Another short delivery and it is an action replay of the first ball. Buttler pulls it to fine leg and jogs and completes a run.
Back of a length on off, Curran guides it through backward point to give the strike over to Buttler.
Once again Buttler walks right across his stumps and pulls it down to fine leg for a run.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. One run added to the total.
Eases this through covers and takes a run.

Fires this one on the pads, it is the straighter one. Curran works it to square leg. He sets off for a run but is sent back at the right time by his partner. Marsh there fires it to the keeper who whips the bails off and appeals but the batsman is well in.

Brilliant delivery! This is flatter on off, gets it to turn away from the batsman. Curran does not play for the turn and tries to work it on the leg side. He is beaten by the spin and the ball goes agonizingly close past the off pole.
Slower through the air on middle, Buttler waits for the ball and then works it towards square leg for a quick run.
On the shorter side, Buttler punches it through covers and runs the first one hard. He calls for a second, goes for it and completes it. Good running.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Walks right across his stumps and flicks it through mid-wicket for a run.
This time he does manage to guide it down to third man for a run.
Just outside off, Curran tries to guide it down to third man but gets it off the bottom part to the keeper.
Back of a length on off, Curran keeps it out.

OUT! The cross-seam delivery does the trick. Stoinis strikes and Australia get the start they would have wanted after the break. It is on a length around off, bounces a touch more and also moves away a touch. Moeen Ali tries to play across the line but closes the face of the bat a bit early. The ball takes the leading edge and goes into the hands of the point fielder. Lyon there takes a simple catch. England slip further and Australia only 4 wickets away from avoiding a whitewash.
Brings the reverse sweep out and this time he connects well. The fielder at sweeper cover runs to his left and makes a good sliding stop. Two taken by the batsmen.
Loopy ball on off, Buttler hits it hard but finds the fielder at mid off.
Eases this down to long off for a run.
In the air... but safe! The dots almost paid off. Ali goes for the conventional sweep. He gets a top edge which lands towards deep square. No fielder there and the batsmen get two.
Opens the face of the bat and guides this towards point for another dot!
Flatter on middle, Ali defends it towards covers.
A single to end a good first over by Stoinis! Ali pushes this through covers and runs to the other end. 125 more needed.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Attacks the stumps this time on middle, Ali defends it out.
BEATEN! Get in a slip, Paine! Another short ball outside off, Ali throws the kitchen sink at it but does not connect.

EDGED but no slip in place! You are defending a paltry total, you have your opposition's half the side back. You should be having a slip. Stoinis bowls it on a length around off, Ali goes at it with hard hands. He gets an outside edge through the vacant slip cordon. Stanlake in the deep runs to his right, dives and keeps it down to two.
Lands it on a length around off, Ali defends it to point.
Marcus Stoinis is into the attack.
Fires it on middle, Buttler blocks it.
The batsman has played it towards mid-wicket. One run added to the total.
Strokes it through covers and takes a run.

Lucky again is Buttler! He goes for the reverse sweep to a ball which is outside off. He misses. The ball hits his body and it seems to be going onto the stumps but his bat once again makes contact with the ball on his followthrough and it goes away from the sticks behind.
With the turn works it to short fine leg.
Uses his feet but Lyon sees that. He shortens his length on middle. Buttler tries to flick but misses to get hit high on the pads.
Shuffles across and also takes a step across the stumps. Stanlake bangs it short outside off, Buttler guides it down to third man and retains strike for the next over.
Goes fuller this time on off, Ali eases it to the man at sweeper cover for another single. The English batsmen are content in taking singles at the moment.
Back of a length on off, Ali pushes it to covers.
A bumper on the body, Buttler swivels and pulls it towards fine leg. Does really well to not lose his balance and fall over onto the stumps. Then, he calls for a run and completes it.
Slightly short but not the bounce he wanted. Ali off his hips tucks it through square leg and gets to the other end.
Hits the length hard on off, Ali off the back foot keeps it out.
Fires it on middle, Buttler goes back and keeps it out. Another tight over comes to an end.
Flighted ball on off, Ali strokes it through covers and takes a run.
Works it around the corner with the turn and gets to the other end.
Very full on off, the spin is out of contention. Buttler drives it to mid off.
Good by Moeen! This is tossed up again on off, this one does not turn. Moeen taps it towards covers and gets to the other end. Rotating the strike will be very important.
PEACH! Turn, bounce that delivery had everything. Floats this one up on off, it turns away sharply and also bounces. Ali tries to keep it out off the front foot but gets beaten.
Now, Stanlake offers width outside off, Buttler stays back to cut it through the line but fails to middle it properly. Finds point and that ends a tidy over. Just one coming off it.
Tries to manufacture something, Jos. He steps out and across to create room but Billy sticks to his line around off. It's bowled on a length and once again Buttler only ends up defending it back.
On a good length this time, around off, Buttler presents a straight bat in defense. Giving respect to the bowler in form.
Good line from Billy. Not offering enough room as he continues to operate around off with a shortish length. Excellent pace as well. Buttler is forced to defend back.
Shortish and on off, Buttler leans back a bit and plays it down to point.
Back of a length delivery around middle and leg, Moeen gets on his toes and taps it down on the leg side for a run.

Billy Stanlake, the star with the ball, to operate from the other end. He bowled with a lot of fire in his first spell where he bagged three wickets and Australia will be hoping for more from him. No slip though for him. Hmm...
Continues from around the wicket and serves a loopy full ball on off, Buttler decides to stay back in defense.
Tossed up ball on off, Moeen stays back and guides it through the gap at cover-point for a run.
Quicker one, probably an arm ball around off, Moeen defends it from the inner half of the bat to the leg side.
Uses his feet to get down the track and forces it past the bowler towards mid on. Lyon acts to stop the ball and mimes a throw at the striker's end as the batsmen cross.
Full and flighted on off, bringing the batsman forward, Buttler dead bats it.
Starts with a shortish ball around off, Buttler plays it late but finds the short third man fielder.
The players are back on the field! It's going to be Nathan Lyon to continue from this end. 140 needed off 204 balls. Let's play.
...THE CHASE RESUMES...

In spite of doing all the hard work thus far, do not be surprised if England canter through to a win. Why so pessimistic, do you ask? Because the main effort has been put in by the lanky Stanlake. The visitors need to stem in a team performance and not just expect Stanlake to pick up the remaining wickets. England might be 5 down but they are just one good partnership away from a whitewash. Meanwhile, psst psst... Panama have managed to score a goal against England in the FIFA World Cup - ensuring that it will not be a clean sheet for England. Can Australia do the same here in cricket and avoid a whitewash? Join us back at 1515 local (1415 GMT) for the remainder of this run chase...

Often, while defending small totals you need your opening bowlers to fire. Roy did that for Australia, giving Ashton Agar his wicket and then Billy Stanlake broke through that middle order. His fiery spell - 3 wickets in 5 overs, which also included a double-wicket maiden and 21 dots - had the English batsmen hopping. Lyon and Agar were not bad too, keeping the pressure on England. There is not much pressure chasing totals just over 200 in an ODI game, but these days, many batsmen consider 4 dot balls in an over as 'PRESSURE'.

Were England a bit too careless in their approach to 206? Sometimes that does happen. Such targets which can put you in trouble if you play too cautiously. Maybe, the hosts wanted to make a statement and in that process, ended up giving wickets away. Nothing to be taken away from Australia, who, barring Richardson have ensured that they were not caned.

Probably the most entertaining passage of cricket in this entire ODI series. England are tottering at 66/5 and all wickets have been lost in the span of an hour. Of course, 3 have been thrown away but make no mistake, Australia have bowled well.

A high full toss to end the 'session'. Buttler pulls it towards long leg and nearly gives a catch to Billy Stanlake over there. Lands just short. A single taken. 11 runs from that over which takes ENGLAND to 66/5, NEEDING ANOTHER 140 RUNS!!!
FOUR! PLUNDERED! Short and outside off, Buttler crashes it to the point boundary.
The batsman dances down the track but decides to defend it.

IN THE AIR... JUST WIDE AND FOUR!!! Heart-in-mouth moment for Buttler and England. Richardson bowls the cutter, outside off and Buttler, who is ages early in his push, is foxed by the change in pace. Spoons it towards short extra cover where Travis Head flies to his right but the ball goes through.
Clips this through mid-wicket and returns for a brace.
Around off, Buttler walks down the track and defends.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Full and outside off, driven straight towards mid off.
Outside off, pushed towards cover for a run.

RUN OUT CHANCE MISSED! Well, that could have tilted the game in Australia's favour. Moeen ticks it towards mid-wicket and sets off for a risky single. Travis Head charges to the ball from square leg, picks it up and has a shy at the bowler's end, only to miss. Lyon chose not to collect the ball, else Moeen would have been gone. Probably Ali mistook Travis Head's throwing arm. He is a left-hander, Travis and perhaps Mo thought he will not throw well with his 'wrong' hand. The ball meanwhile, has gone towards sweeper cover and Ali wants the overthrow but Buttler has run too far and rejects it.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Full on middle, pushed towards mid on.
Nathan Lyon to bowl probably the final over before the break.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. One run added to the total.
Another leading edge, this time from Buttler, looking to flick and this one went past point. Another run taken.
On a length on middle, Moeen looks to flick but gets a leading edge towards third man. A single taken.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
On a length outside off, angling away, left alone.
Moeen Ali walks in at number 7, replacing Hales.

OUT! Loose, loose shot with Lunch around the corner! Totally needless from Hales. Yes, a bad ball from Richardson. Short and wide outside off, there to be hit but without any footwork? Naah... Hales just throws his bat at the ball with his feet probably in clay. Only manages a nick behind and Paine does the rest. Hales walks off fuming as England lose half their side...
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover. The crowd cheers again! ENGLAND 6-0 UP IN RUSSIA!!!
The batsman works it down the leg side. They pick up a single.
Full and around off, watchfully defended out.
Pushes it through the covers for a run.
Outside off, dabbed to short third man.
Full and outside off, driven past a diving Nathan Lyon at short extra cover for a single towards long off.
FOUR! Up and over! Full and outside off, Buttler goes hard and lofts it over mid off who was inside the circle.
Full and outside off, driven towards mid off.
Outside off, Buttler pushes it towards point.
Around off, coming in with the angle, watchfully defended.
Walks down the track and nearly spoons a catch to Aaron Finch at short mid-wicket. Eludes him and the ball goes towards mid on.
Full and outside off, driven through the covers for a brace.
Kane Richardson comes on to bowl now.
Full and outside off, pushed through the covers for one more.
On middle and leg, flicked fine for a run.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Pushes this past the bowler towards long off for a single.

INSIDE EDGE, FOUR! Slice of luck for England. Agar tosses this one around off and Buttler lunges to defend. But the ball comes in with the angle, takes the inside edge and just misses the stumps en route the fine leg fence!

When did you last see this? Two Powerplay 2 signals in the span of a scheduled single innings. POWERPLAY 2 has been signalled. 4 fielders allowed outside the 30-yard circle till the... well, 40th over, if the match lasts till then.

FOUR! A tiring delivery from the tall man. Shot and outside off, Hales crunches it through point and gets a boundary. Not a bad way for England to end what has been Australia's Powerplay - 4 wickets picked, only 34 runs given and only 4 balls reached the fence.
Pushes this towards mid off once more.
Full and outside off, driven towards mid off.
Pushes this behind point and takes a run.
On a length outside off, Buttler feels for it away from his body and nearly nicks it behind.
Outside off, dabbed towards third man for a single.
Another one played in that region.
Short again, cut straight to point.
Full and outside off, driven back to the bowler.
Outside off, short in length, cut straight to point.
Full again, driven towards long off. Short extra cover dives to his right, but misses. Then mid off dives, he too misses. Mid on cannot get around to his left in time either.
Full on middle, flicked towards short mid-wicket.
Ashton Agar is back on. 3-0-11-1 so far.
Outside off, coming in, comfortably left alone. A WICKET MAIDEN FOR STANLAKE whose figures read 4-1-12-3!!!
Outside off, pushed towards cover.
Jos Buttler comes in at number 6, replacing his captain.

OUT! Timberrrrr! Stanlake is on fire and Australia are trying to make this into a contest. Morgan commits a bit too early into the shot, jumping down the track, then as is his habit, going back to defend. Stanlake fires in a quick delivery, landing it on a length and then skidding it through. The skipper tries to cover his initial juggling foot movement by a back foot defense but is totally done in by pace. The ball goes through before the bat can come down, hits the flap of his right pad and then deflects onto the woodwork.
Around middle, pushed towards cover.
A bouncer slightly down the leg side, Morgan ducks.
On a length on middle and leg, defended towards mid on.
Full and outside off, wristed towards mid on.
Very slow, full again, outside off, AH is forward early but has to wait for the ball to come. Eventually defends it towards cover.
Much fuller, around off again, Alex defends it by coming forward.
A touch shorter, around off, worked straight to mid on.

FOUR! SUBLIME! Full and outside off, Hales leans and drives it past a diving short extra cover to the boundary behind! Moves to 11 from 12 balls with his second boundary. 179 more needed from 262 balls.
Short and outside off, cut straight to point.
Captain Eoin Morgan walks in at number 5, replacing Root. There is a bowling change as well, with Paine going to Nathan Lyon.

OUT! Edged and gone! Boy o boy, Australia have their third. This is a well-deserved and a well-thought out wicket. Root has been having trouble with the short ball outside off and Stanlake produces exactly that. Root looks to push that to the off side but the extra bounce proves to be his downfall. All he manages is an outside edge, straight to Shaun Marsh at first slip. 2 wickets from that over, leaking just 4 runs. Stanlake's figures now read - 3-0-12-2.
Short and outside off, Hales cuts it through the covers. Travis Head gives it a good chase, gets to the ball and then flicks it back in. Three runs taken.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Gets off the mark with a flick towards fine leg for a single.
Around off, watchfully defended.
Joe Root walks in at number 4, replacing Bairstow.

OUT! Chops it on! Australia have their second wicket before the break. Stanlake bends his back and lands it on a length outside off. Bairstow looks to run it down to third man but the extra bounce does him in. The ball takes the inside edge and cannons into the stumps.
Full and straight, defended back to the bowler.
WIDE. A short ball down the leg side, JB looks to pull but misses and Paine parries it towards short fine leg. A single taken.
Now comes the arm ball, on middle, Jonny clips it behind square leg and charges back for the second. 189 more needed from 271 balls.
Fourth dot ball. Fractionally drops the pace down a bit, lands it outside off, Bairstow punches it towards point.
Outside off, punched towards point.
More cheer from the crowd - ENGLAND GO 5-0 UP IN FIFA! Coming back to cricket, it is a dot ball. Full and around off, defended back to the bowler.
Full and around off, defended watchfully.
Taps this with soft hands towards cover and takes Travis Head on. The fielder has a shy at the bowler's end but misses. Bairstow was in though.
Outside off, punched straight to cover.
Outside off, dabbed behind point for a couple where Short fields and invokes ironic cheers from the crowd. Two runs taken.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.

EDGED, FOUR! Good ball from Stanlake, landing it on a length outside off and making it come back in. Bairstow looks to punch it through the line but is cramped for room and the ball takes the outside edge. However, there is no second slip and the ball races towards third man where D'Arcy Short makes a mess of a simple fielding effort. Question to Paine - With nothing to lose, why isn't the slip cordon packed?
Short and outside off, Bairstow slashes but misses.
Full and straight, driven back to the bowler.
Short and outside off, cut straight to point.
FOUR! Now the cheers are for a cricketing shot. Full on middle, Hales comes forward and wrists it wide of mid on and the ball goes all the way.

Another arm ball, on leg stump, this time Jonny stays leg side of the ball and drives it towards long off for a single. There is a massive cheer around the ground - not for the single, but because ENGLAND HAVE GONE 4-0 UP IN THEIR FIFA match against Panama.
The arm ball, around middle, pushed back to the bowler.
On middle and leg, grips a fraction, Bairstow pushes at it with hard hands and the ball lobs in the air for a while before reaching the short mid-wicket fielder on the bounce.
Full on middle, swinging away, Alex covers the line nicely and pushes it towards mid on.
Tight line, in line of the stumps, Hales blocks it back.
On middle and leg, clipped through mid-wicket for a single.
Outside off, punched straight to cover.
Outside off, left alone.
On a length around off, watchfully defended.
Billy Stanlake to bowl with the second new ball.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground. A decent opening over from Agar.
On middle and leg, watchfully defended.
Alex Hales walks in at number 3, replacing Roy.

OUT! Well, that is yet another wicket which has been thrown away today. Australia threw away 9 out of their 10 wickets and now Jason Roy makes sure England have at least one contribution. Tossed up on middle and off, Roy comes down the track, is nowhere near the pitch of the ball and just swings wildly. Misses and the ball hits the timber. Some solace for Australia - they have managed to dislodge the opening stand early this time.
Full and outside off, driven gloriously yet powerfully towards long off for a run.

JUST SHORT! Full and around off, Roy plays that a tad uppishly and nearly spoons a return catch. Agar dives to his left but cannot get to the ball. It goes past him towards mid off and the batsmen take a single.
Around off, defended from the crease.
They are back! Well, Paine is starting with a spinner. It will be Ashton Agar vs Jason Roy first up. Jonny Bairstow is the other batsman. Here we go...
